stories.headline: PKK peace process stalls as MİT prepares technical roadmap for disarmament and DEM Party presses for concrete steps
stories.summary: Turkey's 'Terörsüz Türkiye' Kurdish reconciliation process dominated the week's news. MİT chief İbrahim Kalın briefed AKP leadership on a technical roadmap for processing PKK fighters who disarm — covering surrender logistics, weapons disposal, and a verification mechanism for returnees. AKP maintained its sequencing demand (disarmament verified before legislation), while DEM Party escalated criticism calling the government 'hesitant and evasive.' Erdoğan and PKK commander Karayılan both made public statements about the process; Öcalan commented on his 'status' question. The Cabinet meeting scheduled for 5 May was expected to review process progress.

stories.headline: İmamoğlu IBB corruption trial continues: 15 defendants released, İmamoğlu denied floor, wife speaks out
stories.summary: The Istanbul Metropolitan Municipality (IBB) corruption trial at Silivri entered its 29th-30th sessions during the week. Fifteen defendants including Adem Soytekin (who gave evidence of repentance) were released; İmamoğlu's request to address the court on his release bid was denied by the judge; his wife Dilek İmamoğlu made an unusually forceful statement outside the courthouse; and a government minister responded at an international transport conference when İmamoğlu's letter was read aloud.

stories.headline: CHP holds 107th protest rally in Karabük, launches nationwide 81-province field campaign
stories.summary: CHP held its 107th consecutive 'Millet İradesine Sahip Çıkıyor' protest rally in Karabük on 3 May, with CHP leader Özgür Özel addressing crowds on İmamoğlu's imprisonment, early elections, mining pollution, and Gazze's Sumud Filosu. Separately, CHP announced a 4 May nationwide field mobilization with all top party officials simultaneously canvassing voters across 81 provinces, explicitly framing it as the start of its electoral campaign.

stories.headline: New polling shows Erdoğan trailing İmamoğlu, Yavaş, and Özel in all presidential match-ups
stories.summary: An Ankara Research and Consultancy poll of 2,004 participants published this week showed CHP as the leading party and Erdoğan losing to all three prospective opposition candidates — İmamoğlu (55.6% vs 44.4% after undecideds distributed), Yavaş (56% vs 49%), and Özel — in hypothetical presidential scenarios. A separate PİAR poll found 21.3% of AKP voters would not back the party without policy changes. Commentary focused on the implications for the planned 2027 November elections.

stories.headline: AKP launches 2027 election preparation drive, Erdoğan instructs party overhaul targeting lost voters
stories.summary: Multiple reports based on AKP internal sources indicated Erdoğan ordered the party to formally begin 2027 election preparations, with a focus on recovering lost voters rather than recruiting new ones. Party structure is being overhauled, with inactive provincial figures being replaced. Separately, reporting linked Erdoğan to instructing Finance Minister Şimşek on a mid-year wage increase package for retirees and minimum-wage workers ahead of elections.

stories.headline: Turkey Municipalities Union elects CHP's Vahap Seçer as president amid İmamoğlu letter brawl
stories.summary: The Turkish Municipalities Union (TBB) held its general assembly and leadership election. CHP's Mersin Mayor Vahap Seçer won with 446 votes against AKP-backed Fırat Görgel (311). A physical altercation broke out when a CHP delegate attempted to read a message from imprisoned Istanbul Mayor İmamoğlu; AKP members objected and a scuffle ensued, with the meeting briefly suspended. İmamoğlu subsequently congratulated Seçer via his presidential candidacy office.

stories.headline: May Day protests: over 500 detained in Istanbul as Taksim remains banned zone
stories.summary: Turkish authorities detained over 500 demonstrators on 1 May as workers attempted to march to Taksim Square in Istanbul. The crackdown came one day after Turkey's Constitutional Court ruled that 58-day detentions of protesters at the 2024 May Day demonstration violated the right to peaceful assembly. TKP-organized rallies also took place in Ankara, İzmir, and Adana.

stories.headline: Turkey unveils broad investment and tax competitiveness package, pitching Istanbul as regional financial hub
stories.summary: On 27 April, Turkey unveiled the 'Türkiye Yüzyılı: Yatırım İçin Güçlü Merkez Programı' — a comprehensive package including steep corporate tax cuts (to 14% for exporters), incentives for talent and capital attraction, FX conversion support, and positioning Istanbul as a regional financial center. Finance Minister Şimşek was the public face of the announcement. Business associations called for further corporate tax reductions.

stories.headline: Finance Minister Şimşek announces record annualized exports of $275.8 billion; warns Q2 may show turbulence
stories.summary: Finance Minister Mehmet Şimşek announced April trade data showing exports rising 22.3% year-on-year with annualized exports hitting a record $275.8 billion. He attributed part of the April gain to a calendar effect and warned of possible Q2 volatility from geopolitical pressures. IMF spring meetings featured Şimşek speaking on trade corridor investments. Q1 tourism revenues running at an annualized $65.6 billion were separately noted.

stories.headline: TCMB May agenda: Karahan to brief parliament; inflation report due; gold sales draw NYT scrutiny
stories.summary: TCMB published its May calendar showing Governor Karahan will present to TBMM's Planning and Budget Commission on 5 May, with the second 2026 Inflation Report due 14 May and the Financial Stability Report on 22 May. Separately, TCMB held its annual general meeting where Karahan reaffirmed willingness to tighten if inflation worsens. The NYT reported Turkey sold 120 tonnes of gold (or used it in swaps) since the Iran war, making TCMB the world's largest gold seller in the period — a divergence from other central banks buying gold. Analyst commentary debated whether a June rate cut remains possible.
